  run          Run deterministic registry operations.
  mcp          Run the TypeScript MCP server over stdio.
  update       Update the installed make-docs tool itself.
  uninstall    Remove make-docs' machine-level footprint.

  make-docs --version
  make-docs setup --yes
  make-docs setup reconfigure
  make-docs setup skills --dry-run
  make-docs setup remove --backup
  make-docs resource list

Treat `docs/prd/` as the single active PRD namespace for the repository and archive earlier PRD sets under `.make-docs/archive/prds/`. The active PRD set describes the current authoritative shape of the product; it must never describe the editorial operation used to change that authority. Treat decomposition as a delegation-first workflow because single-agent execution degrades quickly on context-heavy repos. When delegation is available, the coordinating agent is coordination-only and must not author or edit output documents.
11:
12:Inside the make-docs repository, shipped lifecycle assets are authored from the accepted v2 source-of-truth layers: template-owned files start under `packages/docs/template/`, dogfood copies under root `docs/` validate those shipped assets, and project-owned lifecycle artifacts under `docs/designs/`, `docs/plans/`, `docs/prd/`, and `docs/work/` remain local project records. 18:3. Default to planning when the request is broad or when no approved plan exists.

20:5. Read the relevant bundled reference files and skill-local templates before writing docs or delegating work.

1:# Archive Workflow
2:
3:## Purpose
4:
5:Shared authority for the `archive-docs` skill. All modes in this skill defer to this file for workflow rules. Archive structure and the hard "never archive unless asked" rule are authoritative in `.make-docs/archive/AGENTS.md`; this file governs the workflow for getting there.
6:
7:## Archival Modes
8:
9:Mode detection is intent-based: infer the mode from user phrasing and confirm before proceeding.
10:
11:| Mode | Trigger phrases | Behavior |
12:| --- | --- | --- |
13:| **Direct** | "archive this file", "move X to archive" | Archive the named artifact(s) only. No relationship tracing. |
14:| **Related** | "archive this and anything related", "archive the whole chain" | Archive the target plus all upstream, downstream, and lateral relatives. |
15:| **Replacement** | "this replaces X", "archive the old version" | Archive the superseded artifact and link the replacement. |
16:| **Project** | "archive everything for this project", "clean up wave N" | Archive all artifacts sharing a wave/revision scope. |
17:
18:## Relationship Tracing
19:
20:### Upstream Tracing
21:
22:- **Work backlog** — scan `00-index.md` and phase files for links into `docs/plans/`.
23:- **Plan** — scan `00-overview.md` for links into `docs/designs/`.
24:- **History record** — read `coordinate` frontmatter; find the matching plan and work directory sharing the same wave/revision. If older moved records do not have `coordinate`, fall back to W/R/P filename parsing.
25:
26:### Downstream Tracing
27:
28:- **Design** — scan `docs/plans/` for overview files linking back to the design.
29:- **Plan** — scan `docs/work/` for index files linking back to the plan.
30:- **Plan/Work** — scan `.make-docs/archive/history/` for history records whose `coordinate` matches the same wave/revision. If older moved records do not have `coordinate`, fall back to W/R/P filename parsing.
31:
32:### Lateral Tracing
33:
34:- **Any artifact** — scan each effective `docs/assets/<persona-slug>/` for guides with `related` frontmatter pointing to the artifact.
35:
36:### Slug-Based Heuristic
37:
38:When link-based tracing produces no results, fall back to slug matching. A plan with slug `guide-structure-contract` is likely related to a design with the same slug. Use slug matches as candidates, not certainties — always present them for confirmation.
39:
40:## Interview Flow
41:
42:1. **Identify target(s)** — resolve the user's request to one or more concrete file paths.
43:2. **Trace relationships** — run upstream, downstream, and lateral tracing from each target.
44:3. **Present findings** — group results by relationship type (upstream, downstream, lateral, slug-matched) with a recommendation for each (archive, skip, or flag for review).
45:4. **Confirm** — wait for explicit user approval. The user may select all, some, or none.
46:5. **Execute** — move approved artifacts to `.make-docs/archive/` per the sub-directory mapping below.
47:6. **Post-archive link rewriting** — scan remaining active artifacts for broken links and propose rewrites.
48:
49:## Replacement Detection
50:
51:Four signals indicate an artifact has been replaced:
52:
53:1. **Explicit user statement** — the user says "X replaces Y" or "archive the old version."
54:2. **Design lineage** — a design's lineage frontmatter contains `updated-existing`, indicating it supersedes a prior design.
55:3. **Guide deprecation** — a guide's frontmatter has `status: deprecated` with a `related:` field pointing to the replacement.
56:4. **Same-slug heuristic** — a newer artifact exists with the same slug but a different date or wave. Treat as a candidate, not a certainty.
57:
58:## Link Rewriting
59:
60:After archival, scan all remaining active artifacts for links to newly archived files. Transform relative paths from the original location to the archive location. Present all proposed rewrites for user confirmation before applying. Never auto-rewrite.
61:
62:## Staleness Signals
63:
64:| # | Signal | Applies to | Detection |
65:| --- | --- | --- | --- |
66:| 1 | All downstream phases complete | Work backlogs | Every `- [ ]` in every phase file is `- [x]` |
67:| 2 | All downstream work complete | Plans | Every derived work backlog is fully complete per signal 1 |
68:| 3 | All downstream plans and work complete | Designs | Every derived plan's work is complete per signal 2 |
69:| 4 | Status is `deprecated` | Guides for every effective Persona | Frontmatter contains `status: deprecated` |
70:| 5 | Superseded by newer artifact | Designs, plans | Detected via lineage frontmatter or same-slug heuristic |
71:| 6 | No active references | Any | No non-archived artifact contains a link to it |
72:
73:## Deprecation Rules
74:
75:- Add a blockquote notice at the top of the file:
76:  ```
77:  > **Deprecated:** This document has been superseded by [replacement](relative-link). It is retained for historical reference.
78:  ```
79:- For guides with YAML frontmatter, set `status: deprecated`.
80:- Record the replacement path in frontmatter if known.
81:- Do NOT move the file — deprecation is an in-place operation.
82:- Relationship to archival: deprecation is a precursor, not a substitute. The staleness-check skill treats deprecated status as one of several archival signals.
83:
84:## Impact Analysis Output
85:
86:When running in dry-run or impact mode, produce the following:
87:
88:- **Files that would move** — each file with its archive destination path.
89:- **Active artifacts with links to target(s)** — these links would break on archival.
90:- **Proposed link rewrites** — old path to new path for each affected link.
91:- **Guide and history reference count** — number of history records and guides for every effective Persona referencing the target.
92:- **Incomplete downstream warning** — flag if any target has downstream work that is not yet complete.
93:
94:## Archive Sub-Directory Mapping
95:
96:This mapping mirrors `.make-docs/archive/AGENTS.md`. Sub-directories are created on demand, not pre-created.
97:
98:| Artifact type | Archive target |
99:| --- | --- |
100:| Design | `.make-docs/archive/designs/` |
101:| Plan | `.make-docs/archive/plans/` |
102:| Work | `.make-docs/archive/work/` |
103:| PRD set | `.make-docs/archive/prds/YYYY-MM-DD/` |
104:| History record | `.make-docs/archive/history/` |
105:| Maintainer guide | `.make-docs/archive/guides/maintainer/` |
106:| User guide | `.make-docs/archive/guides/user/` |
107:
108:## Hard Rules
109:
110:- NEVER archive without explicit user approval.
111:- Archive structure authority is `.make-docs/archive/AGENTS.md`.
112:- Archived artifacts preserve their original filenames.
113:- W/R naming is preserved when archived (not rewritten).
114:- PRD archives use dated sub-directories; use `-XX` zero-padded increment suffix when the same date repeats.

1:# MCP Playbook
2:
3:## Purpose
4:
5:Use this playbook when `jdocmunch` and `jcodemunch` are available. These MCP servers are the preferred path because they reduce token use, speed up repo inspection, and make parallel decomposition safer.
6:
7:## Preferred Servers
8:
9:- `jdocmunch` for documentation indexing and section retrieval
10:- `jcodemunch` for code indexing, symbol discovery, references, and dependency analysis
11:
12:## Session Rule
13:
14:Configured MCP servers do not prove that the current session can access them. Confirm live session access first, then index.
15:
16:## Recommended Sequence
17:
18:1. Confirm live session access.
19:2. Index repository docs with `jdocmunch`.
20:3. Index the codebase with `jcodemunch`.
21:4. Use indexed search and retrieval for planning or execution.
22:
23:## Documentation Workflow
24:
25:When `jdocmunch` is available:
26:
27:- index the repo root or the docs subtree
28:- search sections before reading full docs
29:- use section-level retrieval to inspect decomposition plans, existing PRDs, and other internal docs
30:
31:## Code Workflow
32:
33:When `jcodemunch` is available:
34:
35:- resolve the repo and inspect the outline or tree first
36:- use symbol search, file outlines, references, and dependency graphs before broad raw reads
37:- use raw file content only when indexed views are insufficient
38:
39:## Parallel Agent Rule
40:
41:MCP indexes are session-scoped for this workflow. If execution uses spawned agents or parallel workers, each agent must:
42:
43:1. confirm live MCP access in its own session
44:2. create its own indexes
45:3. proceed with its assigned scope only after indexing
46:
47:Do not assume the coordinator's indexes are visible to spawned agents.
48:
49:## Fallback Workflow
50:
51:If one or both servers are unavailable:
52:
53:1. Recommend the missing servers to the user.
54:2. Ask whether to proceed without them.
55:3. Fall back to local repo exploration with fast tools such as `rg`, `find`, manifest inspection, and targeted file reads.
56:4. Keep the same output contract and doc templates.
57:
58:## When To Re-index
59:
60:Re-index when:
61:
62:- a long execution span changes the repo materially
63:- a spawned agent starts a new session
64:- the current session loses index state
65:- the plan expands from one repo area into the full codebase
